overview: This Senate resolution honors two Iowa Army National Guard soldiers, Sergeant William Nathaniel 'Nate' Howard and Sergeant Edgar Brian Torres-Tovar, who were killed on December 13, 2025, near Palmyra, Syria. According to the resolution, they were taking part in a counter-terrorism mission against remnants of the Islamic State when a lone gunman believed to be tied to the group opened fire; a U.S. civilian interpreter was also killed and three other Iowa Guard soldiers were wounded. The resolution honors the two soldiers' service, offers sympathy to their families, praises the troops and partner forces who responded, and condemns the attack. It asks that copies be sent to both families. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on December 18, 2025.
for: Supporters say the Senate should formally honor service members killed in the line of duty, recognize their families' loss, and condemn attacks on U.S. troops.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law, policy, or spending, including on the U.S. military mission in Syria.
